newsitem.title: USA: FBI agents say Oklahoma witness confident.
newsitem.headline: FBI agents say Oklahoma witness confident.

text.p: FBI agents and sketch artists Wednesday described a key prosecution witness as "confident" when he identified Timothy McVeigh as the man who rented a truck believed to have been used in the Oklahoma bombing.

FBI special agent Raymond Rozycki told a pre-trial hearing auto mechanic Tom Kessinger was confident and clear during a sketch drawing. "He did not go back and forth. He was very clear on his selections."

Attorneys for defendants McVeigh and Terry Nichols want the testimony of certain eyewitnesses excluded from the upcoming trials, arguing they may have identified McVeigh because they saw his picture on television.

Kessinger has identified McVeigh as the man who came into Elliott's Body Shop in Junction City, Kansas, on April 17, two days before the bombing, to rent a Ryder truck. Sketch artist Jean Boylan said Kessinger had told her he was "fixated" with the man renting the truck because he appeared to be chewing tobacco on both sides of his mouth and that fascinated him.

"The witnesses have been absolutely consistent in their testimony that the person who rented the Ryder truck on April 17, 1995 was the defendant, Timothy McVeigh," prosecutor Scott Mendeloff told reporters outside the courthouse.

But the defence has attacked Kessinger's credibility because he has admitted making a mistake about the mysterious "John Doe No. 2," whom Kessinger originally thought had accompanied McVeigh to rent the truck. That person later turned out to be Todd Bunting, who came into the shop to rent a truck the following day, prosecutors have said.

Another issue defence attorneys are focusing on is the discrepancy between McVeigh's actual height and the figures witnesses gave to investigators. McVeigh was measured in prison in bare feet and was found to stand 6 feet, 1/2 inch, compared with estimates from witnesses at Elliott's of 5 feet 10 inches to 5 feet 11 inches.
Officials records gave his height as 6 feet, 2 inches, and Mendeloff said the latest measurement puts the "witnesses much closer to the actual height of McVeigh."

McVeigh and former army buddy Terry Nichols are accused of bombing the Alfred P. Murrah federal building in Oklahoma City in April 1995, killing 168 people. McVeigh's trial begins March 31 and Nichols will be tried at a later date.
